findings.reason: the runtime inventory test is the durable guard, not a one-off measurement, so a known blind spot on the exact shape it was built for lets a future worker re-introduce a parameter-taking staged-replace helper unnoticed; the plan should add a clause distinguishing a staging temporary (written-then-renamed, single directory) from a move-aside, or state why that shape cannot recur.
findings.text: §9's inventory rule reports a staged write only when the rename's source is a name bound locally in the same function body, and it explicitly classifies "a rename whose source is a parameter ... a move, not a fork"; that single exclusion is required to spare the dispatch.py move-aside, but it also blinds the permanent runtime guard to a staged-replace helper that receives its temporary as a parameter (def _replace(tmp, dest): os.replace(tmp, dest)), which is the "fork hidden inside a helper" shape §9 exists to catch

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §9 hides the whole staged-write rule (local-binding analysis, os.replace/os.rename/.replace/.rename and bare-name matching, parity with the census) behind one function over the nodes definitions yields, and deletes ~20 private helper forks behind the one _store.py primitive rather than adding wrapper surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan does not fork a shared owner. It names the census as the frozen historical instrument that cannot be imported into the package (docs/research/data), names clones.functions_in as holding token windows and no call node, and promotes reckon/interface_counts.py as the runtime owner, reconciled by a parity assertion rather than a second divergent copy.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §9 adds exactly one public definition (the ported inventory rule on reckon/interface_counts.py) and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and states in its own text that the deleted helpers are private and uncounted, accounting for the net surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §9 searched the codebase, cites the mechanism it extends (reckon/interface_counts.py read_trees/definitions), and names the frozen census predicate (docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233 primitive_concepts) and reckon/clones.py functions_in as rejected alternatives with verifiable reasons; I confirmed each claim against the code.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no wrapper layer: migrating sites become a direct call to the promoted primitive with their payload as the render callback and their private helper is deleted; the surviving paid_lanes.write_document_atomically is pre-existing and already delegates.
